summary.intent: Drive Callisto (Rust release manager for Cargo/npm/PyPI) toward v1 by opening stacked PRs for decision-free fixes, then fixing commit-signing problems, getting PRs merged, and continuing with T06 PR 2 (reject the colon package-reference form).
summary.outcome: 16 fix PRs were opened, their 17 unsigned commits re-signed and force-pushed, and 15 PRs merged. #267 was rebased to resolve its conflict with #266. T06 PR 2 (E316 colon rejection across config, changeset, pre.json and CLI inputs) passed `just ci` at 92.78% coverage and was committed signed and pushed as a ready-for-review PR.

repo: Release owner is derived (first release id by ecosystem priority Cargo > npm > PyPI) and sealed by the intent digest; no persisted owner field exists.
`just ci` includes a 90% coverage gate, a 40-line limit on the simple workflow template, pinned trycmd help text and insta snapshots; changes to these surfaces require updating the pinned outputs.
The CI coverage job does not install Verdaccio, pypiserver or cargo-http-registry, so tests that fail on missing tools under CI need `CALLISTO_ALLOW_MISSING_TOOLS=1` there.
Fake git runners in graph tests assert exact args, so new git probes (`rev-parse`, `grep`) need those fakes taught to answer them.

Package references are parsed across about 15 surfaces (changeset frontmatter, pre.json keys, add/matrix/release --package, fixed/linked groups, [[package]] match, [[package-set]] match, product-package and artifact package). Output already emits only the slash form.
Colon rejection is specified as E316, and a bare config reference as E317, in docs/projects/V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json and ADR 12.
The native GitHub stack CI trigger only fires for PRs in a native stack or targeting main.
Two PRs that each append tests to the end of the same test file conflict even when logically independent (#266/#267).

code.finding: PackageId::parse tries the ':' prefix branch before the '/' branch; this is the root parser behind every colon-accepting surface.
resolve_native_with_fallback was the only colon emitter, formatting ambiguity candidates as `eco:name`; it was switched to slash.
PackagePattern::parse looked for ':' before '/' with an explicit comment keeping it; this was made slash-only.
parse_release_selection accepted colon and normalised it to a ReleasePackageId, and its error text recommended the colon form.

workflow: Commit with plain `git commit` and signing on. Copying `-c commit.gpgsign=false` from test-fixture repos silently produced 17 unsigned commits that blocked merging.
A background task's completion notification reports the wrapper's exit code, not the command's. Check the `exit=` line in the log.
zsh parses `$var:refs` as a modifier (use `${var}:refs`), unquoted `%G?` globs, and does not word-split unquoted variables; macOS `sed -i` differs from GNU. Python edits or quoting avoid these.
Re-signing can be done in a scratch worktree with a tree-identity check, then force-pushed with `--force-with-lease` on the old tips.
Merge-testing PR heads pairwise is a cheap way to decide which PRs actually need stacking.
Subagent hand-back reports can be wrong about the codebase and should be verified before relying on them.
Open PRs ready for review, not as drafts.

friction: Unsigned commits were discovered only after the user noticed, requiring a re-sign and force-push of all 16 branches and a rerun of CI.
The first hosted CI run on #261 failed because the coverage job lacks the real-registry tools.
Clippy failed on single-element loops after the colon-test conversion, so `just ci` had to be rerun.
The background-task notification reported exit 0 while `just ci` had actually failed.
Many test fixtures used colon-form input, so converting them to the slash form was laborious.
The 40-line workflow limit, pinned help text and fake-runner arg assertions each caused CI failures.
Group resolution initially swallowed E316 and needed a fix to surface it.
I had previously told the user wrongly that the E101 spec and code disagreed.
open_items: T06 PRs 3 to 5: canonical-required config (E317), canonical CLI arguments, canonical emission.
Decision-free CI work not started: MSRV job, scheduled `cargo deny` plus Cargo dependabot, semver-checks in CI, fuzz targets for manifest editors, edition 2024/resolver 3, panic hygiene.
T12 local TLS registry harness and production-path devpi/Verdaccio tests.

Owner decisions pending: OIDC trusted publishing (needs a policy exception for `id-token`), which crates go to 1.0, pre-release mode on the managed route, snapshot publishing and dist-tag policy, schemaVersion bump, E176/E157 detail carry, foreign-version and wrong-commit tagging.
Release PR #248 and the in-progress Release run on main are awaiting the user's decision to ship.
NEXT-WORK.md still needs shipped items removed and stale ADR/README pre-v1 language fixed.
The four retired crates have not been deprecated (parked by the user).
Maturin support, co-located with Cargo, is deferred until after v1.
The preferred native stack links between PRs were not verified after the force-push.
Hosted CI results for the new E316 PR and #267 had not yet been confirmed.
